title: The Elders of Pumbedita
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 17b they said that they are Rav Yehudah and Rav Eina. They are mentioned in Eruvin 79b, and Rashi explains there: Rav Yehudah and his academy. In Pesachim 117b Rava said: “I found the elders of Pumbedita” (Rav Yehudah and Rav Eina — Rashbam). Hyman finds Rashbam’s words very difficult: how could Rava say this about Rav Yehudah? Hyman’s firm explanation is that Rav Yehudah’s academy, even after his death, was called by his name, since he was its founder; as we find in Avodah Zarah 48a, “Ameimar said: The elders of Pumbedita told me,” and it is known that Ameimar lived many generations after Rav Yehudah.

Likewise in Chagigah 13a: Rav Yosef was studying the Work of the Chariot, and the elders of Pumbedita were studying the Work of Creation. They said to him: “Let the Master teach us the Work of the Chariot.” He said to them: “Teach me the Work of Creation.” After they taught him, he did not want to teach them the Work of the Chariot. Hyman argues that this cannot describe Rav Yehudah.

notes.text: Hyman distinguishes the continuing academy from its founder to address Rashbam and the Ameimar chronology. This argument and his impossibility claim about Rav Yosef’s teachers remain his, not a new generational harmonization.

Sanhedrin 17b directly glosses the elders of Pumbedita as Rav Yehudah and Rav Eina. Hyman’s continuing-academy explanation and his objections based on Rava, Ameimar and Rav Yosef remain his chronological argument, not a new identification of every occurrence.
